The Washington Commanders shouldn't have been able to knock off the Seattle Seahawks without Jayden Daniels in the lineup. Marcus Mariota and Co. did. The Cleveland Browns aren't supposed to have a winning record at this point. They do, with Deshaun Watson leading the way. Kirk Cousins was serving as the bridge quarterback to this year's No. 1 overall overall pick, Fernando Mendoza. He's currently playing like the old Cousins, and the Raiders are undefeated. These examples are exactly why Bleacher Report grades every quarterback performance each week to see how the position continues to progress across the league.
articles.body:
The NFL is unpredictable, because every week of play is a fresh start. This fact also applies to the quarterback position. The Washington Commanders shouldn't have been able to knock off the Seattle Seahawks without Jayden Daniels in the lineup. Marcus Mariota and Co. did. The Cleveland Browns aren't supposed to have a winning record at this point. They do, with Deshaun Watson leading the way. Kirk Cousins was serving as the bridge quarterback to this year's No. 1 overall overall pick, Fernando Mendoza. He's currently playing like the old Cousins, and the Raiders are undefeated. These examples are exactly why Bleacher Report grades every quarterback performance each week to see how the position continues to progress across the league.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

Score : 36-30 loss vs. San Francisco 49ers

Stat Line : 38 of 52 for 280 yards, two touchdowns and a rushing score

Jacoby Brissett has been asked to shoulder too much responsibility since taking over as the Arizona Cardinals' QB1. He's thrown 40 or more passes in eight times over the franchise's last 15 contests. That number jumps to 11 when the bar is slightly lowered to 35 attempts.

Conversely, Brissett's 5.6 yards per attempt ranks dead last among quarterbacks who have started all three games this season. Arizona can move the ball, but the Cardinals lack explosive plays, which makes their lives far more difficult when facing a talented opponent.

Arizona compounded problems Sunday with 10 penalties for 86 yards.

"Against good teams, it's like being a death wish," Brissett told reporters . "Against good teams, you can't do that. You can't beat yourself and try to beat them."

Stat Line : 18 of 25 for 256 yards, a touchdown and an interception

The Atlanta Falcons sat on the edge with the team starting into the pit of despair after a 0-2 start. Kevin Stefanski's squad was staring at the possibility of losing its third game during a primetime contest against the Green Bay Packers. Instead, Michael Penix Jr. made his first start of the season and provided exactly what the Falcons needed.

After a shaky start, where Penix threw an interception, the third-year quarterback grew more comfortable with each passing offensive possession. He missed four of his first five passes, then completed 17 of his final 20 attempts.

"He wanted to get back out here when he felt comfortable [after last season's ACL injury], and I respect that," Falcons running back Bijan Robinson told reporters . "He looked comfortable [Thursday], and he was balling."

Stat Line : 15 of 20 for 186 yards and two touchdowns; six carries for 50 yards

The Baltimore Ravens found themselves in a second-half shootout with the Dallas Cowboys and emerged with a last second victory thanks to a 56-yard Tyler Loop field goal. But it's what led to that final kick which made the outcome more impressive.

A 27-yard connection between Lamar Jackson and Zay Flowers led to the field-goal attempt. The Ravens pieced together the scoring drive in six seconds. It's the quickest game-winning drive in NFL history.

"It is something we have been practicing since camp," Jackson told reporters . "We were practicing it almost every day after camp, probably mixing [it] in practice sometimes. We were surprised because we did not go over that all week. We were not expecting to be in a situation like that, but [offensive coordinator Declan Doyle] called the play. Everyone was on the same timing."

In total, the Ravens and Cowboys combined for 35 second-half points.

Score : 24-16 win vs. Los Angeles Chargers

Stat Line : 16 of 26 for 204 yards, two interceptions and a fumble lost; eight carries for 22 yards and two touchdowns

Josh Allen is human after all. The Buffalo Bills quarterback performed like the best football player on the planet during the first two week of the 2026 campaign. The Bills were forced to come back from a 10-point first-quarter deficit in Week 3 to ensure a 3-0 start. Allen needed plenty of help thanks to his three-turnover performance.

In total, the Bills had five turnovers, committed 10 penalties and lost the time-of-possession battle.

"You're not going to win very many games turning the ball over that much," Allen told reporters . "Sometimes the ball bounces the other way. That's what happens. ... We've got to clean a lot of stuff up."

Stat Line : 26 of 48 for 291 yards, a touchdown and an interception

The Carolina Panthers offense was flying high through the first two weeks of play. The unit set a franchise record for points scored to start a season and ranked among league's top five offenses. The Cleveland Browns defense made life miserable in Week 3, though.

Cleveland sacked Young three times and hit him on eight different occasions. The Browns pressured the quarterback on 30 of his 47 dropbacks, according to Syed Schemes' Tej Seth . Carolina struggled significantly in high-leverage situations, too. Young and Co. finished a combined four for 18 during their third- and fourth-down attempts.

Young still helped his squad gain a fourth-quarter lead. In the end, the third-year quarterback was pressured, had his arm hit and threw an interception to end the squad's hopes. He didn't come out of the game unscathed, either.

"Yeah, there were a couple of ball he'd normally hit," head coach Dave Canales said when asked about Young battling through a lower-body injury. "I'm wondering if he was working through something to find his base and get those balls out. He can make those throws."

Score : 30-27 loss vs. Pittsburgh Steelers

Stat Line : 28 of 37 for 282 yards, three touchdowns and a fumble lost

Joe Burrow is the solution for the Cincinnati Bengals. Too bad his teammates continue to create problems.

For example, a blown one-on-one block by right guard Dalton Risner led to a sack that caused Burrow to fumble and ended the team's chances to emerge with a victory.

"Guys got to take ownership of their roles, got to take ownership of themselves, and just be smart situational football players," Burrow told reporters after the game.

The quarterback added , "Self-inflicted. Just like last week with the penalties, we just can't shoot ourselves in the foot like that. You can't win in this league when you do that. It's really hard. It's really hard. We could have overcome it, but it's really hard to win like that."

As Locked on Bengals' Jake Liscow noted , Burrow continues to deliver in crunch time. Others let him down.

Stat Line : 16 of 30 for 144 yards and two touchdowns; 11 carries for 45 yards

Deshaun Watson can breathe easier this week. Back-to-back victories will certainly alleviate pressure for the Cleveland Browns to replace their current starting quarterback. Furthermore, the team's fanbase didn't turn on its QB1. Instead, the preseason boos turned into cheers.

"There was one moment, I got teary-eyed," Watson told reporters . "I was just feeling that energy. I put so much work into getting back here. To be in this moment here. To be able to show, I can finished these drives, finish these games and get Ws for the city and the organization." Watson didn't perform as well as a passer compared to his Week 2 outing. In fact, he completed 53.3 percent of his attempts. However, his ability to extend the play and find open receivers when it mattered helped lift the Browns to their first 2-1 start in three years.

Stat Line : 25 of 40 for 276 yards and a touchdown

Dak Prescott did enough to eventually win Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens. However, the Dallas Cowboys' coaching staff made a tactical error by having Brandon Aubrey kicked the ball into the end zone after the team's game-tying field goal.

In doing so, the Baltimore Ravens got the ball at the 35-yard line without any time running off the clock. Two plays later, the Cowboys had lost, with a long flight home from Brazil awaiting them.

Though Prescott looks at it differently. The Cowboys did tie the game, which should have gone into overtime. However, Dallas failed to score a touchdown on its final drive despite having the ball inside the Ravens' 5-yard line.

"Frustrated as hell. Embarrassed," Prescott said after the game . "We don't call ourselves the best offense, 'GOTI,' and we get down there to the 1-yard line and don't put it in. It just sucks. Not a lot of words or full explanation of it. Defense shouldn't have even been in that position. Those guys are over there saying, 'It's on us.' Absolutely not. We've got to put the game away, period."

Stat Line : 17 of 34 for 186 yards, two touchdowns, rushing score and an interception

Move over Jim Harbaugh. The Denver Broncos' Bo Nix is now deserving of the "Captain Comeback" nickname after leading yet another Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams.

Since the start of the 2025 campaign, Nix leads the NFL with seven fourth-quarter comebacks, nine game-winning drives and 20 touchdowns when trailing by a score, according to NFL Researcher .

Of course, Nix and Co. have to dig themselves into a hole before securing a second-half victory. The Broncos quarterback threw for 53 yards during Sunday's first half, and the Rams owned a 16-0 lead going into intermission.

However, a different version of Nix shows up as the game progresses.

"A [basketball] shooter might miss three shots or whatever," wide receiver Courtland Sutton told reporters , "but once they see that one go in, it allows them to have that confidence to keep shooting. And then next thing you know, they look up and they've got 30 points. So I think that you have to have that shooter's mentality, and our mindset is trying to figure out a way to make that first one go in faster."

Stat Line : 25 of 32 for 269 yards and two touchdowns

Jared Goff was perfect against the New York Jets. Specifically, the Detroit Lions quarterback finished 14 of 14 passing when facing the Jets' blitz packages .

Goff serves as the archetype as a distributor in today's NFL. His understanding of Detroit's system, where to go with the ball and post-snap decision-making is exactly what a team wants in its quarterback. The Lions' signal-caller may not provide much more, but he's fantastic at what he does.

"I thought it was just a headsy, smart game," head coach Dan Campbell told reporters about Goff's performance. "... He was just being patient with it. Then, he started to hit some [deeper shots]. ... We put a lot on him, and he's just playing at a high level."

Stat Line : 28 of 53 for 312 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

The Green Bay Packers offense is a mess, and Jordan Love isn't doing anything to make it better.

First, the Packers' offensive line is beset by injuries. Two new starters were in the lineup Thursday. The group allowed only one sack. However, the Atlanta Falcons generated 12 quarterback hits.

Second, Green Bay's ground game is basically non-existent. Matt LaFleur's squad already fielded the league's worst rushing attack through the first two weeks. The Falcons held them to 17 rushing yards. Finally, Love isn't performing well.

"I think to start, my footwork in the pocket. I think making accurate throws, my decision-making and reads, going through those things quickly. I think just the feeling I have right now is not good," Love told reporters . " … There's always going to be plays where there's going to be pressure. Sometimes you might have a little more time in the pocket, but as a quarterback, I've got to operate a lot faster and be more accurate and find completions to help us as an offense."

Score : 19-17 loss vs. Indianapolis Colts

Stat Line : 16 of 27 for 167 yards and a touchdown

CJ Stroud is failing the Houston Texans and vice versa.

The Texans entered this season with the knowledge that Stroud reached the point in his career where a contract extension could be on the table. But the organization still didn't know whether the 2023 second overall draft pick deserved consideration as a franchise quarterback.

Through three games, Stroud hasn't looked the part. The team's 0-3 start isn't doesn't fall solely on its quarterback, of course. The Texans once again didn't properly address their offensive interior, which makes life even more difficult on Stroud. Unless another turnaround occurs, like it did after last season's 0-3 beginning, the Texans may have to reconsider their options.

"These are the types of games we're supposed to win," Stroud told reporters . "We fought, but, at the end of the day, there's a lot of things that need to be fixed."

Stat Line : 24 of 36 for 235 yards, a touchdown, an interception and two lost fumbles

Daniel Jones wasn't good enough, yet the Indianapolis Colts found a way to beat the rival Houston Texans. Shane Steichen's squad hasn't been able to say that for some time.

Indianapolis' last-ranked defense came to play and held the Texans to 223 yards. Jones made some difficult throws, particularly under duress. But a trend has emerged through the first three weeks where the veteran quarterback's decision-making comes into question, his ball-handling is suspect and turnovers occur. Jones has produced at least one turnover in three straight games, with three during Sunday's contest. He didn't have a similar stretch at any point last season.

"Obviously, you cant turn the ball over like that," Jones told reporters . "I can't put the team in that position. I certainly understand how important that is as a quarterback. But the game goes on and you gotta move on, play the next play and execute."

Score : 35-6 win vs. New England Patriots

Stat Line : 19 of 29 for 182 yards, three touchdowns and an interception

Trevor Lawrence's maturation as an NFL quarterback became apparent when he broke free toward the end zone and kneeled at the 1-yard line instead of scoring a touchdown so the Jacksonville Jaguars could milk the clock in the fourth quarter.

"When I broke free and nobody tackled me, it's something we talk about all the time, potentially, in those situations to keep the clock running," Lawrence told reporters . "That was too much time (left) when I looked at the clock and saw eight minutes left. But I was just trying to use as much clock as possible and give [the New England Patriots] as few chances as possible to get back into the game." Lawrence didn't need to put up huge numbers thanks to the New England Patriots' mistake-filled performance. At the same time, he threw for three scores and understood situational football. His one turnover even came off a defended pass.

Stat Line : 20 of 24 for 246 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

Patrick Mahomes holds himself and his team to a high standard and rightly so. At his very best, Mahomes can make a strong argument as the greatest quarterback of all time. So, a two-touchdown victory against the Miami Dolphins didn't necessarily make Mahomes happy.

"I have to continue to work the pocket and find places to throw," the two-time NFL MVP told reporters . "That's about me finding my feel for the pocket in some of those critical situations. ... We have to get better as an offense. ... We're not going to be mad about winning, but we're going to look at the tape hard and find ways to get better next week."

The Kansas City Chiefs' play-action passing game is one area where everything is clicking. According to ESPN Insights , Mahomes completed all 14 of his play-action passing attempts Sunday.

Score : 35-27 win vs. New Orleans Saints

Stat Line : 22 of 33 for 248 yards and three touchdowns

Fernando Mendoza may not see the field during his rookie season, not when Las Vegas Raiders remain undefeated and Kirk Cousins is tied for the the NFL lead with nine touchdown passes.

The Raiders find themselves in the best-case scenario, where the veteran bridge is playing like a legitimate starting quarterback and this year's No. 1 overall pick isn't being rushed onto the field.

According to Shawn Syed of Sumer Sports , Cousins posted the highest EPA when pressured over the last two weeks of play. The Raiders quarterback definitely benefited greatly from Brock Bowers return to the lineup Sunday. Bowers caught 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown.

"He's an outstanding player," Cousins said during a postgame interview . "Klint [Kubiak] did a great job with the scheme to give him opportunities. I'm still learning him. We don't have as many banked reps as I would like. But I think I can get accustomed to a guy like that pretty quickly."

Stat Line : 20 of 34 for 226 yards, a touchdown and an interception

The Los Angeles Chargers have been a disaster to start this season. Mainly, the team's offense has been disappointing.

Mike McDaniel's hire this offseason was supposed to open up the offense and make life easier on quarterback Justin Herbert. Instead, the opposite has happened. No one appears to be on the same page.

During McDaniel's time as the Miami Dolphins head coach/offensive play-caller, his team was known for its vertical passing attack. Herbert has one of the NFL's biggest arms, yet he's not connecting with targets down the field. According to NFL Researcher , Herbert has completed only two of 12 pass attempts of 20-plus air yards. To make matters worse, three of the quarterback's interceptions have come during those throws.

"That's something that we have to figure out," Herbert responded when asked why the offense continues to play poorly.

Stat Line : 30 of 55 passing for 390 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions

Will the real Matthew Stafford stand up? Last season, Stafford played the quarterback position at a higher level than anyone else. This year, the 38-year-old veteran has been far more inconsistent.

Stafford can still put up numbers, as evidenced by 390 passing yards against the Denver Broncos' defense. He did so without top wide receiver Puka Nacua in the lineup. At the same time, Stafford is making decisions and throws he shouldn't.

Sunday's contest turned on a Talanoa Hufanga pick-six. Stafford threw another interception on the final play of the game as well, which Hufanga also snagged. Both turnovers occurred when pressured. Stafford completed only nine of 23 passes when the Broncos were breathing down his neck, per Sumer Sports' Shawn Syed . His four interceptions are tied for the league's second-most through three weeks of play.

Score : 24-10 loss vs. Kansas City Chiefs

Stat Line : 20 of 36 for 210 yards, an interception and a fumble lost; nine carries for 56 yards

Said Brooks , "I think we fought until the end. We had a chance to win that game. The next step for us is learning how to win those games." The Dolphins find themselves in an obvious evaluation season, and quarterback Malik Willis doesn't have the help around him to prove whether he's a legitimate long-term starter. Miami already lacked offensive weapons. The Dolphins' best offensive player, De'Von Achane, suffered a knee injury Sunday. As a result, Willis led the team with 56 rushing yards. Beyond that, the quarterback really doesn't have the necessary pieces around him and his play suffers.

Score : 23-16 win vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Stat Line : 15 of 29 for 168 yards, a touchdown and an interception

Kyler Murray made a full debut Sunday as the Minnesota Vikings' starting quarterback. The former Arizona Cardinal experienced a false start in Week 1 due to a concussion. Now, Murray is at the helm of the 3-0 Vikings and brings different much-needed qualities.

Murray certainly wasn't perfect against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He completed just over 50 percent of his passes and threw a tipped interception. However, his ability to run and drive the ball deep are both positives. As for the latter, Murray completed all three of his first-half deep passes for 93 yards, including a 41-yard touchdown connection with Jordan Addison, per NFL Next Gen Stats .

Minnesota has gotten off to an undefeated start thanks to its aggressive defense. Murray has the potential to unlock the offense and allow the team to play complementary football.

"Let's call it what it is: We're going to need to play better on offense to be the type of team that I think we can become," head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters .

Score : 35-6 loss vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Stat Line : 14 of 25 for 199 yards, two interceptions and a fumble lost

Drake Maye looks completely lost through the first three weeks of play. Last season's MVP runner-up is a shell of the performer that helped lead the New England Patriots to a Super Bowl. Now, he's a hindrance.

Maye turned the ball over three times against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Since the start of last season's postseason (seven games), the 24-year-old signal-caller threw 10 interceptions and fumbled nine times, according to CBS Sports' Doug Clawson . The belief in what Maye is seeing and letting throws rip simply isn't evident.

"Try to show him the looks. Try to give him, me personally, I try to talk to him about just taking the ball and putting it where it's supposed to go," head coach Mike Vrabel stated when asked how he can help Maye. "... He's a young quarterback. I want him to go and be energetic and talk to him about can't be a robot here. We got to go. And we saw some times where he extended plays and kept his eyes downfield or made plays, and then also we just can't turn it over at the rate that we're turning it over, especially down in the red zone."

Score : 35-27 loss vs. Las Vegas Raiders

Stat Line : 29 of 42 for 255 yards, four touchdowns, an interception and two fumbles lost

Tyler Shough is talented, but he's yet to piece together a complete full-game effort this season.

All of the physical tools and capabilities are present. The second-year second-caller must become more consistent, though. Furthermore, three turnovers in one game is simply too many. It's the second time this season that Shough had as many giveaways. Unsurprisingly, the New Orleans Saints lost both contests.

Shough keeps the team competitive. At the same time, he's missed opportunities.

"We're just a couple of plays away," the quarterback told reporters . "... We can clean that up for sure. There's a lot of stuff we can learn from, including finishing strong, and that starts with myself protecting the ball."

Jameis Winston didn't do enough for the New York Giants to beat the Tennessee Titans. That's OK. He didn't to.

The Giants benefited from a ground-and-pound approach, a strong defensive effort and multiple Titans mistakes. Tennessee didn't pieced together a drive longer than three plays until the team's seventh offensive possession. Winston simply needed to avoid a significant mistake, which he did.

"Jameis did what was required in this game," head coach John Harbaugh told reporters . "The first thing you have to do is what's necessary, what's required. After that, then you can do what's possible. Then maybe the impossible becomes possible."

As a result, Winston will remain the Giants' starting quarterback.

Stat Line : 31 of 37 for 321 yards, three touchdowns and a fumble lost

Geno Smith has been everything the New York Jets hoped he'd be and more. He doesn't even look like the quarterback from last year, when he was arguably the worst starter.

Smith made multiple pinpoint passes Sunday against the Detroit Lions, because his targets on all three touchdowns didn't have much, if any, separation. Unfortunately, his performance was marred by a poor outing by the New York Jets' offensive line, which surrendered five sacks.

Still, the Jets are highly competitive, because their veteran quarterback is playing well.

"It makes it really easy to play receiver," rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq told reporters . "He's a great quarterback."

Score : 30-27 win vs. Cincinnati Bengals

Stat Line : 19 of 34 for 292 yards, three touchdowns and an interception

Aaron Rodgers can still get the job done. He simply needs help, which he hasn't necessarily gotten through the first two weeks of play. The Pittsburgh Steelers offense looked different in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals.

The Steelers' front five gave Rodgers time. According to ESPN's Benjamin Solak , Rodgers average time to throw Sunday was the highest he joined the Steelers. In turn, the veteran quarterback pushed the ball down the field more often, with 15 attempts of 10 or more air yards.

"We had some explosion in the offense back, especially in the run game," Rodgers told reporters . "We did better on third downs, so we had more opportunities." Jaylen Warren's 127 rushing yards helped created a perfect symbiotic relationship for the Steelers to maximize the offense's potential.

Stat Line : 15 of 27 for 297 yards and four touchdowns

At this very moment, the San Francisco 49ers' Brock Purdy is playing the quarterback position better than everyone else.

As The Ringer's Sheil Kapadia noted , Purdy produced this season's two highest EPA-per-pass-play performances during the last two weeks. Currently, the Niners' signal-caller is tied for the league-lead with nine touchdown passes. His 93.8 QBR and 133.1 quarterback rating is first among his contemporaries. Purdy is operating Kyle Shanahan's offense at the highest level.

"Kyle's confidence in Brock is incredibly high," tight end George Kittle told reporters . "Brock's confidence is incredibly high. It's different. We can be in a Wednesday practice and Brock might miss a pass, and, I think, in years past, Kyle would be frustrated with him for not hitting that pass.

"Now, Kyle is like, 'Nah, he'll hit it on game day.' It's fun to see that."

Score : 33-31 loss vs. Washington Commanders

Stat Line : 31 of 45 for 379 yards, four touchdowns and two interceptions

The Washington Commanders ruined Sam Darnold's return to the Seattle Seahawks lineup. Darnold missed the second week of the season after suffering a glute injury early in the team's season debut. During Sunday's contest, he looked too much like the version that predated his time in Seattle.

To be fair, the quarterback didn't receive much help. Seattle's ground game managed only 44 yards. Jadarian Price, Emmanuel Wilson and George Holani averaged 2.3 yards per carry. As a result, Darnold's 45 pass attempts were his most since joining the Seahawks.

While Darnold put up significant numbers and threw four scoring passes, each of his second-half interceptions led to Washington touchdowns, including a pick-six. Seattle wouldn't have been competitive Sunday if not for Darnold. He also give the Commanders too much.

Score : 23-16 loss vs. Minnesota Vikings

Stat Line : 17 of 34 for 217 yards, a touchdown and an interception

The start of the 2026 campaign couldn't have gone worse after the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and quarterback Baker Mayfield agreed to a three-year, $165 million contract extension just before the season began. Now, the team is sitting at 0-3 and Mayfield will miss time due to a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand.

According to The Athletic's Jayna Bardahl and Jeff Howe , Mayfield is expected to be out at least three weeks.

Prior to the injury, Mayfield was under constant duress. The Vikings sacked the Bucs' quarterback six times and hit him on 12 occasions. He's pressed all season, trying to be a playmaker, which has led to mistakes and the injury.

Upon his return, Mayfield must be smarter with his decisions and work within the structure of Tampa Bay's offensive scheme. Despite the team's awful start, no one is running away with the NFC South again.

Stat Line : 23 of 36 for 181 yards, one touchdown and an interception

Regression is a strong word when describing Cam Ward's play, because he only showed so much as a rookie.

Last year's No. 1 overall pick incrementally improved throughout his initial campaign. However, he never showed the level of play that warranted high expectations going into Year 2. His performance through the first three weeks certainly hasn't inspired hope. Instead, questions about whether he should remain QB1 were asked after Sunday's contest.

The Tennessee Titans had an opportunity to win their matchup with the New York Giants despite play poorly for the majority of the contest. On 1st-and-goal from the 7-yard line and 24 seconds left to play, Ward scrambled to his left, didn't see an underneath defender and threw an interception. He had a near-interception dropped during the Titans' first trip into the red zone.

"He needs to be smarter with the football," head coach Robert Saleh said after the game . "We had two timeouts left. ... You don't need to force it in that situation."

Stat Line : 19 of 31 for 183 yards and three touchdowns

After the disappointment from last week's loss against the Dallas Cowboys and Jayden Daniels' injury, the Washington Commanders responded against the Seattle Seahawks. Backup-turned-starter Marcus Mariota was a big reason why.

"The more that adversity hits, the more that the circumstances kind of pin us against the wall, these guys find a way," Mariota said after the game . "I'm grateful to be a part of it."

Mariota has actually been the better option for Washington over the last season-plus. As the Philly Voice 's Jimmy Kempski noted , Mariota has a slightly better completion percentage, higher average yards per attempt, more touchdown passes and a higher QB rating despite both starting the same amount of game since the start of the 2025 campaign.

Obviously, Daniels can be a dynamic playmaker when he's healthy. But Mariota is more than capable of keeping the team afloat, even against a good defense like the Seahawks.

articles.title: Madison Beer Opens Up About 'Magical' Engagement to Justin Herbert
articles.summary: It hasn't been a great start to the season on the field for Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers, but the quarterback has a "magical" engagement off it.
articles.body:
It hasn't been a great start to the season on the field for Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers, but the quarterback has a "magical" engagement off it.

As Ashlyn Robinette of People relayed, Beer called her engagement to Herbert "magical" during a Twitch stream and explained he proposed to her on their one-year anniversary of dating on July 26.

"Very cute," she said. "My heart can't take it. Honestly, it makes me want to cry whenever I talk about it. But it was on our one-year of being official. We had been together, obviously, before he asked me to be his girlfriend, but it was on our official one-year anniversary."

The couple announced their engagement on Instagram two days later.

For his part, Herbert told SiriusXM NFL Radio in training camp Beer has "changed my life."

The engaged quarterback will look to get the Chargers in the win column in Week 4 when they face the Seattle Seahawks following an 0-3 start to the campaign.

articles.title: Grading J.J. McCarthy NFL Trade Between Giants and Vikings
articles.summary: As many expected, J.J. McCarthy's time with the Minnesota Vikings has come to an end. He'll look to revive his career prospects with the New York Giants.
articles.body:
As many expected, J.J. McCarthy's time with the Minnesota Vikings has come to an end. He'll look to revive his career prospects with the New York Giants.

According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , the Vikings traded McCarthy to the Giants for a 2027 fifth-round pick.

Minnesota will move Max Brosmer into the No. 3 quarterback spot on the depth chart, while Big Blue adds another young quarterback in the absence of Jaxson Dart, who's out for the season with MCL, PCL and meniscus injuries.

This is a logical trade, given the circumstances for both teams and McCarthy. Here are grades for the clubs and the player based on immediate and potential long-term impact.

J.J. McCarthy's time in Minnesota had clearly run its course. After starting in 10 games, throwing for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions, he lost the starting job to Kyler Murray in an offseason competition.

In Week 1, Murray suffered a concussion. Yet the Vikings turned to Carson Wentz over McCarthy as their primary backup, an indication that the young signal-caller had lost a position battle and fallen on the depth chart.

Keep in mind that former Vikings general manager Kwesi Adofo-Mensah selected McCarthy with the No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 draft. Minnesota fired him weeks after the 2025 season. Ironically, the club dismissed him five days after former Vikings signal-caller Sam Darnold helped lead the Seattle Seahawks to Super Bowl LX.

The Vikings saw Darnold, a quarterback who flourished under head coach Kevin O'Connell, become a stable starter and Super Bowl champion. In the same year Minnesota signed Darnold, it drafted McCarthy, who sat out his rookie campaign with a knee injury.

Darnold's ascension in Seattle coupled with McCarthy's struggles in Minnesota doomed Adofo-Mensah, though the Vikings didn't see a long-term path for the 23-year-old signal-caller either.

Even though O'Connell told reporters that he believed McCarthy had a "future with the organization," it didn't seem that way once Wentz surpassed him on the depth chart.

Minnesota traded its third-string quarterback for an early Day 3 pick, which doesn't match the cost of what it invested in McCarthy, but it's better than what most teams would get for a signal-caller at the bottom of the pecking order.

The Giants gave the Vikings an escape from their failed draft pick. In the short term, this deal makes sense if McCarthy eventually usurps Jameis Winston as the backup. Otherwise, he becomes a long-term developmental player.

This past offseason, the Giants signed Winston to a two-year extension. So, their new coaching regime trusted the 12-year veteran enough to give him a multiyear contract, which means he'll likely continue to start in the coming weeks.

Moreover, don't expect the Giants to thrust a struggling young quarterback into a lead role for a 2-1 team that hasn't folded for the season. Although Winston has had turnover issues, McCarthy does too, with more limitations.

According to The Athletic's Alec Lewis , Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell had to reduce his playbook to help McCarthy last year.

"In 2025, Minnesota also removed most of its over-the-middle passing concepts throughout the season to keep his line of sight as simple as possible," Lewis wrote back in February.

The Giants would likely insert McCarthy into their starting lineup for one of two reasons. Either Winston goes down with an injury, or their season has run off the rails, which signals a time to give developing players valuable snaps.

J.J. McCarthy has a much better shot at playing with the Giants than he did with the Vikings. Even though Big Blue signed Jake Haener over the summer, the former fourth–round pick from the 2023 draft doesn't have as much upside as a recent top-10 pick.

We've seen former first-rounders revive their careers with new teams, and McCarthy can do the same. But with only 10 career starts, he needs regular-season experience and an organization committed to his development.

According to former New York Daily News reporter Gary Myers , Giants general manager Joe Schoen considered drafting McCarthy with the No. 6 overall pick in the 2024 draft, but instead, he selected wideout Malik Nabers.

Myers also noted that Jim Harbaugh and John Harbaugh often work with the same players. McCarthy won a national championship with the former at Michigan in 2023.

Because of those coaching ties, the Giants may show more commitment to McCarthy's development than the Vikings, who fired the general manager tied to him.

Lastly, McCarthy plays more like Jaxson Dart than Jameis Winston does. He can move in and out of the pocket and make off-script plays. The Giants' coaching staff must help him with ball placement, layering his throws and mechanics for easier completions, though.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: Patriots HC Vrabel Sends Message to Maye, 'Stop Trying to Choke the Life Out of Every Single Play'
articles.summary: New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel believes quarterback Drake Maye would benefit from simplifying things on the field and getting out of his own head.
articles.body:
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel believes quarterback Drake Maye would benefit from simplifying things on the field and getting out of his own head.

Appearing on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show , Vrabel said broadly that "quarterbacks want to make plays" when asked about Maye. He went on to make a golf analogy to discuss what might be going wrong with the MVP runner-up.

"I think sometimes when Greg and I go golfing, we really want to make a good score, right?" Vrabel said. "Sometimes we're so focused on it that we try to choke the life out of the golf club, and we're squeezing it so damn tight that the ball has no choice but to go sideways.

Cowboys HC gives himself an F after loss to Ravens

"We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play. We need to relax. We need to settle in and go play football and not try to force things that aren't there."

Speaking with the media, the coach said he wants to strike a "great balance" between perhaps making the offense simpler while adding some new wrinkles:

Through three games, the Patriots are 22nd in average yards (307.0) and tied for last in points (12.0).

The performance of Maye has been the biggest head-scratcher. He has thrown for 585 yards, one touchdown and a league-high six interceptions.

A.J. Brown's ankle injury undoubtedly has something to do with how badly New England's offense is faring. Much was expected of the star wide receiver, and he has logged a total of 31 snaps.

Maye managed to make do pretty well without Brown in 2025, though. There's a marked difference between how he looked in the pocket last year versus now.

Perhaps a lot of it is mental. Maye had a clunker in a Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks and has started putting more pressure on himself to improve, which has the opposite of its intended effect.

A Week 4 matchup with the Buffalo Bills provides the Patriots with an opportunity to rebuild their confidence. The overall vibes around the team will lift if New England takes down one its strongest challenger for the AFC East crown.

Conversely, a loss to Buffalo might raise even more alarm bells in Foxborough.

articles.title: Vikings GM Explains J.J. McCarthy Trade to Giants, Says QB's 'Story is Not Yet Written'
articles.summary: Just over two years ago, the Minnesota Vikings drafted J.J. McCarthy with the 10th overall pick, hoping he could eventually be their franchise quarterback.
articles.body:
Just over two years ago, the Minnesota Vikings drafted J.J. McCarthy with the 10th overall pick, hoping he could eventually be their franchise quarterback.

On Monday, they traded him to the New York Giants in return for a fifth-round pick.

Despite the trade, Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley had high praise for his former quarterback.

"We still have a ton of respect for J.J. Appreciate his professionalism since I've been in this building and even within this situation specifically, sitting down and talking with him this morning, he's a pro," Teasley said (2:05 mark). "He's a great young man. He's a good person. He's a great teammate and I continue to believe that his story is not yet written in this league and that he has the potential to continue to grow and develop and make a difference in the National Football League."

McCarthy's time with the Vikings got off to a rocky start as he missed his entire rookie year due to a knee injury. Once healthy in Year 2, McCarthy did little to prove that he was capable of being the team's long-term option at quarterback.

In 10 games last year, McCarthy threw for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions, completing just 57.6 percent of his passes. His poor performance under center led to the Vikings signing Kyler Murray following his exit from the Arizona Cardinals.

Murray beat McCarthy for the starting role, and McCarthy was later demoted to the team's third-string quarterback behind Carson Wentz.

"When the situation with the Giants presented itself, we spoke internally — that's coaches, myself, the personnel staff, ownership, everyone together — just in terms of where we are in terms of our roster, where it is currently," Teasley said. "That includes the quarterback room... Ultimately, we came to the conclusion that this was the best path forward and the best decision for the Minnesota Vikings."

The decision to part ways with a still-young quarterback perhaps speaks to the Vikings' belief in Murray moving forward. The 29-year-old suffered a concussion in Week 1 and had to miss Week 2 as well. He led Minnesota to a win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday behind 168 passing yards, a touchdown and an interception.

"A lot of belief in the quarterback room," Teasley said. "We've spoken to that from the beginning: the goal was to build a deep, competitive room, and we've spoken about Kyler's potential in this offense. Still looking forward to that coming to fruition and took some steps forward in that regard yesterday."

Being traded in just the third year of his career is surely a bit demoralizing for McCarthy, but the change of scenery could be exactly what he needs. With Jaxson Dart out for the season, McCarthy will play backup to Jameis Winston and has a much better chance of seeing the field this year.

He's still far from being a starting-caliber quarterback, but he at least won't have to serve as the third-string option as he did in Minnesota.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Injury Update, Latest on Commanders QB's Practice Status Ahead of NFL Week 4
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders received a positive update regarding injured quarterback Jayden Daniels on Monday.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders received a positive update regarding injured quarterback Jayden Daniels on Monday.

Head coach Dan Quinn told reporters that Daniels will return to practice this week as he continues to recover from an elbow injury and will travel to London for a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Daniels, 25, dislocated his elbow just before halftime of the team's Week 2 loss against the Dallas Cowboys. He tripped as he was going into a dropback and put his left arm out to break his fall, bending it awkwardly.

It was the second time he's dislocated that elbow in the past two seasons, also doing so in a Week 9 loss against the Seattle Seahawks last November. He missed three games last season with the injury and ultimately reaggravated it later in the season, causing the Commanders to shut him down for the final four games.

He did not suffer any fractures or ligament issues with his current injury, however, and the Commanders didn't put him on injured reserve.

Washington doesn't need to rush him back, of course, with a solid veteran in Marcus Mariota able to start in his stead. The 32-year-old was excellent in a Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks, throwing for 183 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions.

But a healthy Daniels is one of the most dynamic players in the sport and seriously increases Washington's ceiling. While an exact timeline for his return is unknown, it sounds as though he'll be back sooner rather than later.

Amid a plethora of defensive injuries, including one to Nick Bosa, the San Francisco 49ers are adding some depth to their defensive line.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the team is signing pass rusher Matt Judon to the practice squad, and the veteran has an "early chance for elevation."

articles.title: "Surprising low character": Matthew Stafford faces backlash after appearing to spit near Denver’s iconic 5280 sign

articles.body: Matthew Stafford is facing backlash following the Los Angeles Rams’ heartbreaking loss to the Denver Broncos, but this time, the conversation has little to do with what happened between the lines. Stafford was caught on video appearing to spit as he walked toward the tunnel at Empower Field at Mile High following the Rams’ dramatic 30-26 defeat on Sunday night. The footage, shared by NFL on Prime reporter James Palmer, quickly drew attention online.“Don’t spit in our tunnel”: Matthew Stafford faces backlash after Rams’ Denver lossWhat made the moment particularly notable for Broncos fans was its apparent proximity to the stadium’s “5280” sign, a nod to Denver’s famous Mile High elevation.With reporters asking on social media, “Was that the 5280 sign Stafford spit on?”That question helped fuel a wave of reactions from Broncos fans, with some interpreting Stafford’s gesture as a deliberate slight toward Denver.One reaction bluntly told the Rams quarterback, “Don’t spit in our tunnel, Matthew.” Others criticized the gesture and described it as disrespectful and “classless.”However, there is an important distinction: there has been no confirmation that Stafford intentionally spit on or toward the 5280 sign. The video shows Stafford spitting while walking toward the tunnel, but his precise target or intent cannot be established from the footage alone.Stafford and the Rams had plenty to be frustrated aboutThe postgame moment came after one of the most dramatic collapses of the young NFL season. The Rams entered halftime with a commanding 16-0 lead, only for Denver to storm back in the second half and eventually take the game 30-26. Bo Nix scored the go-ahead touchdown with 47 seconds remaining, before Stafford led Los Angeles into position for one final opportunity.Stafford finished the night with 390 passing yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. One of those interceptions became a pivotal moment when Talanoa Hufanga returned Stafford’s pass 66 yards for a touchdown, giving Denver its first lead of the night.Stafford responded almost immediately, connecting with Konata Mumpfield on a 48-yard touchdown to put Los Angeles back ahead 26-23. But Nix and the Broncos had the final answer.Denver marched 65 yards on its final touchdown drive, with Nix scoring from one yard out to put the Broncos ahead. Stafford then drove the Rams down to the Denver 19-yard line, but Hufanga intercepted his final pass in the end zone to seal the comeback.The viral moment adds another layer to a brutal nightThe Rams’ defeat was already difficult enough after surrendering a 16-point halftime advantage. Now, Stafford’s postgame footage has given fans another moment to debate.While some viewers have interpreted the video as Stafford deliberately disrespecting Denver’s 5280 branding, the available footage does not establish that intent. What is clear is that the gesture occurred as Stafford was leaving the field, and it quickly became a talking point among Broncos supporters.For now, the “5280 sign” connection remains an allegation based on the positioning seen in the video, rather than a confirmed account of what Stafford intended.And after a night in which the Rams let a 16-point lead slip away in one of the NFL’s most dramatic finishes, the viral postgame moment has ensured Stafford’s Denver exit is getting almost as much attention as the loss itself.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: J.J. McCarthy, Jameis Winston, Giants QB Depth Chart Discussed by John Harbaugh After Vikings Trade
articles.summary: The New York Giants offered some insight into the quarterback depth chart on Monday after trading a 2027 fifth-round pick for JJ McCarthy.
articles.body:
The New York Giants offered some insight into the quarterback depth chart on Monday after trading a 2027 fifth-round pick for JJ McCarthy.

Head coach John Harbaugh told reporters that Jameis Winston would remain the starter "for as long as I can see into the future" and McCarthy will be a backup in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals.

Nonetheless, the Giants made the decision to not only trade draft capital for a quarterback, but for a younger player—McCarthy is 23—who was a former first-round pick and former starter for the Minnesota Vikings. If they only wanted a reliable backup, they could have signed a veteran free agent.

Trading for McCarthy feels like a developmental move, whether that's to eventually start him later in the year, try to trade him down the line (he's under contract through the 2027 season, with a team option in 2028) or both. McCarthy thriving in a late-season role could increase his trade potential significantly.

Either way, if Winston struggles, there will be plenty of conversations in New York about whether McCarthy should get his shot at the starting gig.
